newsitem.title: CANADA: FIGURE SKATING-STOJKO WOWS THEM AT CANADIAN CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-STOJKO WOWS THEM AT CANADIAN CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Elvis Stojko still had 10 seconds to go in his four-and-a-half minute freeskate on Saturday when the standing ovation began, but the result at the Canadian Figure Skating Championships was never in doubt.

Stojko nailed an incredible quadruple toe-double toe jump combination early in his Dragon Heart-themed programme and he also landed six triple jumps, including two Axels, to win his third national title.
The 1994 and 1995 world champion was clearly in a class by himself in the 16-man field, scoring 5.8s and 5.9s for technical merit and almost all 5.9s for presentation.
By the time he stepped out of his final spin, all 17,000 fans were on their feet cheering for the skater known as "The Terminator."
Stojko's training mate, Jeff Langdon, took the silver medal, while 1995 national champion Sebastien Britten settled for third place.
There was a major upset as in the pairs as perennial also-rans Marie-Claude Savard-Gagnon and Luc Bradet took gold.

The couple, now coached by 1984 world pairs champion Paul Martini, upset two-time national champions Michelle Menzies and Jean-Michel Bombardier, who literally tumbled to third place, as well as the favourites Kris Wirtz and Kristy Sargeant, who faltered in the final to finish second.
Jennifer Robinson, the 1996 women's champion also was upset, finishing third behind long-time contender Susan Humphreys and little-known Angela Derochie.
Stojko said he intends to turn his performance up a notch in the Champions Series Final in two weeks, where he will face much tougher international competition.
"I'll be bumping it up to a triple axel-triple toe combination in both the short and the long. Add a quadruple toe-triple toe and that would be the pinnacle of that (long) programme," he said.
Stojko said there will be added pressure with the final taking place in Hamilton, just an hour from his Toronto home.
"I'll just be making sure I'm healthy and that it will be fun for me. It's tough to skate in your own country."
